conviction_note: The Q3 order shortfall has been public since 1 October and the company-compiled consensus (26 October, 21 analysts) was cut to 3,388 MW. What the release adds that the market has not seen is the Q3 margin against 526m EBIT, a likely narrowing of the 7-9% FY margin guide against a consensus already at 8.4%, Q3 cash flow, and possibly a new buyback. The small positives (peer Nordex's margin beat and raise, unannounced orders above the cut consensus, buyback cadence) roughly offset the high FY bar. So p_up stays near 50 (52), while abs_move is 8% because this name's observed print-day moves have a median of about 8.4%. The findings sum (+0.5) and the scaled number (+0.32) agree in sign and are both small.

findings.finding: The order shortfall is pre-released and the consensus already cut: announced Q3 intake was 2,754 MW against 4,554 MW expected (1 October), and the company-compiled Q3 consensus is now 3,388 MW. Citi's 'normal' 0.7-0.8 GW of unannounced onshore orders implies about 3.5-3.6 GW, a small upside residual to the cut consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 1 October 2026, the day the shortfall was reported, VWS closed -3.3% (196.15 to 189.70), then +5.5% the next day (Yahoo VWS.CO daily bars). The order line has been traded once already.
findings.original_quote: Vestas har hittills annonserat order på cirka 2,8 GW under tredje kvartalet. Med normalt 0,7–0,8 GW i ej offentliggjorda landbaserade order räknar Citi med en total orderingång på omkring 3,5–3,6 GW, klart under konsensus på cirka 4,9 GW. (Vestas has so far announced about 2.8 GW of orders in Q3. With a normal 0.7-0.8 GW of unannounced onshore orders, Citi expects total order intake of about 3.5-3.6 GW, well below the c.4.9 GW consensus.)
findings.why_not_priced: The miss itself is priced: the consensus fell from about 4.5-4.9 GW to 3,388 MW by 26 October. What is not priced is the unannounced residual. A consensus above 3.5 GW, or a range topping out well above 3,600, would mean it was; the range is 3,100-3,600.

findings.finding: Direct peer Nordex printed a Q3 2026 EBITDA margin of 12.7% (8.0% a year earlier) with revenue +28% and raised its FY EBITDA margin guide to 11.5-12.5% from 8.0-11.0% (ad-hoc 15 October). This points to strong European onshore pricing and execution, which bears on Vestas's onshore Power Solutions margin against an 8.8% Q3 group consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin beats have been rewarded on this name: Q2 2026 (9.4% margin and a guide raise) +19.66% on 2026-08-12, Q3 2025 +14.77% on 2025-11-05 (Yahoo daily bars).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. VWS rose +3.2% on 16 October on 4.6m shares, the day after Nordex's pre-release, and the 26 October consensus postdates it. The residual is the proxy transmission to Vestas's own margin, which only the company can confirm. If fully priced, the consensus would sit nearer 9% than 8.8% for Q3.

findings.finding: The FY bar sits in the upper half of the guide. Consensus FY EBIT bsi of 1,794m on 21,332m revenue is 8.4% against the 7-9% guide (midpoint 8%), and with Q1 127m, Q2 446m and Q3 consensus 526m it implies a Q4 EBIT of about 695m at roughly a 10.5% margin. A Q3 narrowing that is not centred at or above 8.4% would read as a cut to the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide changes move this name hardest. The raise on 2026-08-12 gave +19.66%; the Q3 2025 narrowing (rttnews headline 'narrows FY25 outlook... stock climbs') gave +14.77%; the 2026-02-05 first guide gave -8.67% (Yahoo daily bars).
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is public. What is not priced is where Vestas centres the narrowed range, which only the release says. Calculations: 9M at consensus is 1,099m on 14,693m revenue, a 7.5% margin; reaching 8.4% needs Q4 at about 10.5%, above Q2's 9.4% peak. If the market expected only the midpoint, consensus would sit near 8%.
findings.independence: https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b7e82dddac2d512e1ee533f0aa3de7ca8&lang=en&src=listed (7-9% guide); Q1 127m EBIT from https://mb.cision.com/Public/18886/4344988/8503066e29d0add4.pdf; Q2 446m from https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bfc47dac6643e7f36b68c58e4a405fd72&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: The EUR 400m buyback ends no later than 16 December 2026, and Vestas announced buybacks with Q3 2025 (EUR 150m) and Q2 2026 (EUR 400m), against a FY consensus FCF of 1.2bn. A new programme with Q3 is plausible but is not company-stated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both earlier buybacks came on days that moved +14.77% and +19.66%, but each was bundled with an earnings beat, so the buyback's own effect cannot be separated.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference from cadence, and the market prices a buyback only once it is announced. No public note forecasts a new programme with Q3.

findings.finding: The US Section 232 wind-turbine probe was closed on 22 October 2026 with no new tariff but continuing negotiations. Jefferies read this as prolonging uncertainty over Vestas's US order book, so US order commentary on the call is a two-sided line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 22 October VWS closed +1.6% (187.20 to 190.15) on 3.1m shares, then -2.4% the next day (Yahoo daily bars).
findings.why_not_priced: The decision is public and traded. Only management's read of US order timing is new, and its sign is unknown.
